yā cāsya jantunivahasya vimohinīti māyā vibhorjanuṣi śuddhakubuddhihantrī || 2 ||
vedān sarvāṃstathā sāṅgān sārabhūtaṃ pramathya ca || 5 ||
sa sa cchinnastvayā brahman savitreva tamaścayaḥ || 6 ||
niḥsaṃśayā vayaṃ jātā vede śāstre ca sarvaśaḥ || 7 ||

bhṛguñca mānasān putrān yadā daśa sasarja saḥ ||
dadhyuḥ samutsukāḥ sarve tāṃ dṛṣṭvā varavarṇinīm || 40 ||

tanme kuruṣva lokeśatvaṃ sraṣṭā jagatāṃ yataḥ || 51 ||

nāsuro na ca daityo vā na vidyādhararākṣasāḥ || 55 ||
na guhyakā na vā siddhā na manuṣyā na pakṣiṇaḥ || 56 ||
na te sarve bhaviṣyanti na lakṣyā ye śarasya te || 57 ||
sukhahetuḥ svayaṃ bhūtvā kuru sṛṣṭiṃ sanātanīm || 59 ||
nāmāpi ca gadiṣyāmi yatte yogyaṃ bhaviṣyati || 61 ||
dakṣādayastu sraṣṭāraḥ sthānaṃ patnīñca te daduḥ || 2 ||
kiṃ vācātiviśeṣeṇa sāmānye nāsti te samaḥ || 8 ||
tad vaḥ punātu haripādasa rojayugmamāvirbhavat kramavilaṅghitabhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ || 1 ||
translation: May that pair of Hari's lotus-feet purify you — [the pair] that has appeared, having in sequence crossed the worlds bhūr, bhuvaḥ, and svaḥ.

sanskrit: yā cāsya jantunivahasya vimohinīti māyā vibhorjanuṣi śuddhakubuddhihantrī || 2 ||
translation: And that māyā of the Lord, which is called the deluder of this host of creatures — pure, the destroyer of evil understanding — in the Lord's birth(?), [may she purify you].
I shall proclaim the purāṇa named Kālikā, which consists of eternal knowledge.
The sages, headed by Kamaṭha, having bowed, asked.

sanskrit: vedān sarvāṃstathā sāṅgān sārabhūtaṃ pramathya ca || 5 ||
translation: And having churned all the Vedas together with their aṅgas and [brought out] the essence, …

sanskrit: sa sa cchinnastvayā brahman savitreva tamaścayaḥ || 6 ||
translation: That [doubt] was cut away by you, O Brahmā, like the mass of darkness [is cut] by the sun.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayā vayaṃ jātā vede śāstre ca sarvaśaḥ || 7 ||
translation: We have become entirely free from doubt in Veda and śāstra.
The dharmaśāstra together with its secret portion, which was spoken by the Self-born.
He deluded the ascetic and even the Lord by the form of a virtuous woman.
How did [she] agitate Hara, who had turned his face away from saṃsāra?
How did Hara set his mind on the act of taking a wife?
Was she born as the daughter of Himavat, or how did she come again?
Tell all this in detail, O best of twice-born.
Do this, O lord of sages, O knower of the Self, so that we may know it.

sanskrit: puṇyaṃ śubhakaraṃ samyag jñānadaṃ kāmadaṃ param || 15 ||
translation: [This is] meritorious, auspicious-making, properly giving knowledge, granting desires, supreme.
Asked by him, he then also spoke to the Bālakhilyas.
He spoke to the sage Yavakrīta and to Asita.
Having bowed to the Supreme Self, the discus-holding lord of the world, …
To the gross one, to the one of subtle form, to the one whose form is the universe, to the creator — [homage].
To him whose nature is knowledge and ignorance, to him whose form is time — homage indeed!
To the pervasive one, whose form is the universe, who performs creation, maintenance, and destruction — [homage].
I bow to him — the innermost one, whose form is the supreme light.
He created all creatures — gods, demons, humans, and so forth.
Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, likewise Aṅgiras, and Kratu —

sanskrit: bhṛguñca mānasān putrān yadā daśa sasarja saḥ ||
translation: When he created the ten mind-born sons, including Bhṛgu, …
Then a beautiful woman of lovely form was born in his mind.
She will also be possessed of complete virtues in all three times.
Like a peahen [dancing] with variegated [plumage] in the rains, O best of twice-born, …
It shone like the bow of the lord of the gods, resembling a lovely young moon.
And it shone, trembling, like [the glance] of a frightened doe.
O best of twice-born, hers [brows] were dark, like the bow of the fish-bannered one (Kāma).
Her charms flowed forth as if [falling] from her forehead, like a tilaka flower.
It shone, heart-stealing with its passion, [glowing] with the redness of the bimba-like lower lip.
Her two breasts were as if rising to reach her chin.
O sages, her two dark-tipped breasts were deluding even to the sages.
All saw her waist, comparable to a śakti, [the waist] of the mind-born one(?).
[Her waist was] soft and gentle, like the trunk of a bending elephant.
[Her waist was] intermingled with finger-petal(-like) [lines], like the arrows of the flower-armed one.
[She was] with a perspiring face, long eyes, and a lovely smile.
Having seen her, the creator (Brahmā), rising, thought within his heart.

sanskrit: dadhyuḥ samutsukāḥ sarve tāṃ dṛṣṭvā varavarṇinīm || 40 ||
translation: Having seen her, the beautiful one, all became eager and fixed [their minds on her].
'She will be [something]' — thinking thus, they all became eager.
[He was] one whose hands, eyes, face, and feet are reddish.
Conch-necked, fish-bannered, tall, mounted on the makara —
Charming, rolling his pair of eyes with a sidelong glance, …

sanskrit: taṃ vīkṣya tādṛśaṃ dakṣapramukhā mānasāśca te || 47 ||
translation: Seeing him so [beautiful], they — the mind-born ones headed by Dakṣa — …
They reached supreme eagerness, and their minds became agitated.
Having bowed, the man spoke, his neck bent in humility.

sanskrit: māṃ nyāyye puruṣo yasmāducite śobhate vidhe || 50 ||
translation: O Vidhi, since a man shines in a proper and fitting [position], [place] me [there].

sanskrit: tanme kuruṣva lokeśatvaṃ sraṣṭā jagatāṃ yataḥ || 51 ||
translation: Make me [attain] lordship of the world, since you are the creator of the worlds.

sanskrit: kṣaṇaṃ na kiṃcit provāca svasṛṣṭāvapi vismitaḥ || 52 ||
translation: For a moment he said nothing, astonished even at his own creation.
Brahmā spoke to the man, declaring the purport of that task: …

sanskrit: mohayan puruṣān strīṃśca kuru sṛṣṭi sanātanīm || 54 ||
translation: Deluding men and women, make the eternal creation.

sanskrit: nāsuro na ca daityo vā na vidyādhararākṣasāḥ || 55 ||
translation: No asura, nor daitya, nor vidyādharas or rākṣasas —

sanskrit: na guhyakā na vā siddhā na manuṣyā na pakṣiṇaḥ || 56 ||
translation: No guhyakas, nor siddhas, nor humans, nor birds —

sanskrit: na te sarve bhaviṣyanti na lakṣyā ye śarasya te || 57 ||
translation: None of them will become targets of your arrow —
We shall be under your control — what use are other living beings?

sanskrit: sukhahetuḥ svayaṃ bhūtvā kuru sṛṣṭiṃ sanātanīm || 59 ||
translation: Having yourself become the cause of happiness, make the eternal creation.
You will always be the cause of intoxication and joy for all living beings.

sanskrit: nāmāpi ca gadiṣyāmi yatte yogyaṃ bhaviṣyati || 61 ||
translation: And I shall proclaim a name for you which will be fitting.
Seeing [him] well-seated on his own lotus seat, in a moment he became [delighted].
Thus, in the venerable Kālikāpurāṇa, the first chapter, 'The Appearance of Kāma', [ends].
Then Marīci, Atri, and the others gave him that fitting name.

sanskrit: dakṣādayastu sraṣṭāraḥ sthānaṃ patnīñca te daduḥ || 2 ||
translation: And the creators headed by Dakṣa gave him a place and a wife.
The best of twice-born spoke what was fitting to that man: …
Therefore you will be famous in the world by the name Manmatha.
Therefore, O mind-born one, be famous also by the name Kāma.
Then he will be famous in the world also by the name Kandarpa.
And of the Vaiṣṇava, Raudra, and Brahmā weapons — of such a kind — …

sanskrit: kiṃ vācātiviśeṣeṇa sāmānye nāsti te samaḥ || 8 ||
translation: What need of much speech? In ordinary things there is none equal to you.
Here and there let your station be, up to the abode of Brahmā.
Indeed the first Prajāpati who, O best of men, [acts] as desired — …
She will be celebrated in all the world by the name Sandhyā.
Therefore, in this world her fame will be — [the name] 'Sandhyā'.
Having looked at Brahmā's face, he bowed low before [him].
[The arrow] celebrated as 'Unmādana' (the maddening one), with a wave like the brows of a beloved —
[The arrows] Harṣaṇa, the one named Rocanā, Mohana, and likewise Śoṣaṇa —
Concealing his form, right there he formed a resolve: …
I shall do it right here, in the presence of the sages and of Vidhi.
This very speech which was just now spoken by Brahmā — even concerning Sandhyā — …
'What use are other creatures?' — I shall carry out that [resolve] in full.
He strung the flower-string of the flower bow with arrows.
Then Kāma, the archer, bent [the bow] into a full circle.
The best of sages there, causing complete delight, …
The deluder (Kāma) deluded them one by one with his flower arrows.
Deluded in mind, at first they underwent a slight transformation.
Their passion grew great, because she was a woman who increases passion.
Just as those transformations of the senses [came about], they experienced them; so he made them.
At that very time, forty-nine states arose from [their] bodies.
O twice-born, in Sandhyā, pierced by Kandarpa's arrow, there arose …
Again and again she produced such states as sidelong glances and veiling [of her face].
Making [these gestures] excessively, she shone like a golden river with its waves.
Then, her body filled with radiance, she felt desire.
And the best of twice-born headed by Dakṣa attained agitated senses.
And then Madana placed his trust in Sandhyā for his own undertaking.
'It can be done' — his mind filled with faith, he became [confident].
And he laughed at the mind-born ones together with Dakṣa, mocking them.
The bull-bannered one (Śiva), shaming them, said this, O best of twice-born: …
His brow-region was fixed in intent concentration, he trembled with agitation, and his face resembled the full moon.
